triage_notes: Routing: the feedback names dir24 and refers to 'the current report', Figure 2, Figure 3 and the conclusion, all of which exist only in REPORT.md; it explicitly routes the per-anchor Spearman check to RESULTS.md. No new report filename is requested, so REPORT.md stays the primary report and RESULTS.md the detailed-results file.

'43 x 53 heatmap' vs '52 partners' is consistent, not ambiguous: the grid has all 53 well-trained characters as columns and the 43 letter anchors as rows, with the 43 self-pair cells left blank, so each anchor still has 52 partners.

'Replace or supplement Figure 2' is explicitly the author's choice; the feedback also permits keeping the class-median summary 'as a smaller accompanying panel'. Plan limit of 3 main figures is preserved by making Figure 2 a heatmap-dominant figure with the class-median summary as a smaller panel.

Feedback bans new grouping scores, regressions, significance tests and composite metrics; existing W / rho / Friedman / permutation p-values may be retained only after the visual and plain-language results.
The three bin numbers quoted in the feedback must be recomputed independently from this direction's artifacts and reported as measured, not copied.

failures: REPORT.md exceeds its declared 1,600-word budget. Exact word counts on four sampled paragraphs give ~15.3 words per line across 103 body/caption lines (~1,580 words of prose alone); adding the title and six headings (~40), Table 1 (~50) and three display equations puts the file at roughly 1,670-1,720 words, and higher under a plain `wc -w`. The report needs substantive curation (the Methods interpolation paragraph and the Figure 2/3 captions both restate material already in RESULTS.md), not marginal trimming.

REPORT.md Result 2 states as fact: 'Pooled over pairs it vanishes, the between-anchor component cancelling it.' The sole support is RESULTS.md section 4.2's between-anchor row, Spearman rho = +0.255 with p = 0.10, which RESULTS.md itself calls 'weak and not significant'. The report presents a non-significant correlation as the explanation for the pooled null result, unhedged, to a reader who will not open RESULTS.md. Either hedge it explicitly (e.g. 'a weak, non-significant between-anchor trend of opposite sign may offset it') or drop it.

REPORT.md Result 2 attributes within-anchor evidence to the wrong figure: 'the trend is weak and explains little of the variation, as Figure 3's scatter shows.' Figure 3 is a pooled J-vs-w scatter and contains no within-anchor structure; the per-anchor evidence is the rho histogram in RESULTS.md Figure 3. A reader following this pointer cannot verify the claim from the figure cited.

The low-JSD conclusion is asserted more strongly than the feedback requested and than the counterfactual supports. The feedback asked that readers 'see that this may be a character-class cluster'; plots/fig3_jsd_vs_width.png is titled 'the lowest-JSD bin is wide because it is almost entirely punctuation pairs' and REPORT.md states 'The excess is a character-class cluster, not an effect of low divergence.' The dashed 'punctuation-punctuation removed' line, which is the visual carrier of this claim, is based on n = 2 pairs in the lowest bin, and neither the figure nor the report annotates that the lowest dashed point is a two-pair average. Hedge the wording back toward the requested phrasing or annotate the n = 2 point on the dashed line.
content.summary: The revision is substantively responsive to most of the feedback: anchors and class medians are defined with the requested `t` -> {a,e,i,o,u} worked example and the 65/53/43 accounting before any aggregate; c_anchor/c_partner replace a/b; Figure 2 is a genuine 43 x 53 raw pairwise heatmap with class-grouped, alphabetically ordered columns, visible separators and labels, blank self-pairs, the class-median box plot demoted to a small side panel, and no 'confusion matrix' language; Figure 3 uses fixed 0.1-wide bins with per-bin n, faint individual pairs and punctuation-punctuation pairs distinguished by shape and colour; the three quoted bin statistics are reproduced (12/0.581, 31/0.360, 78/0.343); and W, Friedman, Spearman and permutation p-values are confined to RESULTS.md after the visual and plain-language results, with the conclusion narrowed to nearly the requested wording. I nevertheless reject on four points. (1) REPORT.md overruns its declared 1,600-word budget: exact counts on sampled paragraphs give ~15.3 words/line over 103 prose lines (~1,580 words) before headings, Table 1 and three equations, putting the file at roughly 1,670-1,720 words. (2) Result 2 asserts 'the between-anchor component cancelling it' as fact, though its only support is a rho = +0.255, p = 0.10 correlation that RESULTS.md calls not significant - a correlation presented as an explanation, unhedged, in the primary report. (3) The same paragraph cites 'Figure 3's scatter' as evidence for a within-anchor claim that Figure 3 (a pooled scatter) cannot show. (4) The figure title's causal 'because' and the body's 'The excess is a character-class cluster' are firmer than the feedback's requested 'may be', and the dashed punctuation-removed line that carries the claim rests on n = 2 in the lowest bin without annotation. Items 2-4 are localized to Result 2 and its figure and need no new analysis to fix.
